# Data dictionary

**File:** `data/raw/VUS_biomarker_cancer_mutation.csv`: 3,410 variants × 30 columns, 13% of cells missing at random.
**Nature of the data:** synthetic. It was generated by `src/data/generate_synthetic_data.py` to mimic a clinical cancer-genetics cohort. It contains no real patients.

> **Loading note:** read with `pd.read_csv(path, keep_default_na=False, na_values=[""])`. Otherwise pandas turns the valid Alcohol_Use level `"None"` into NaN.

| # | Column | Group | Type | Values / range | Meaning | Designed signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Variant_ID | ID | string | VAR00001–VAR03410 | Unique variant identifier | none |
| 2 | Age | Demography | numeric | 18–90 years | Age at genetic testing | weak (pathogenic carriers slightly younger) |
| 3 | Sex | Demography | categorical | Female, Male | Biological sex | noise |
| 4 | Ethnicity | Demography | categorical | White, Black, Hispanic, Asian, Other | Self-reported ethnicity | noise |
| 5 | BMI | Demography | numeric | 16–50 kg/m² | Body-mass index | noise |
| 6 | Smoking_Status | Demography | categorical | Never, Former, Current | Smoking history | noise |
| 7 | Alcohol_Use | Demography | categorical | None, Moderate, Heavy | Alcohol consumption | noise |
| 8 | Family_History_Cancer | Demography | categorical | Yes, No | First-degree relative with cancer | strong |
| 9 | Cancer_Type | Demography | categorical | Breast, Ovarian, Colorectal, Lung, Prostate, Pancreatic | Patient's cancer | noise |
| 10 | Gene | Genomic | categorical | BRCA1, BRCA2, TP53, PALB2, ATM, CHEK2, MLH1, MSH2, APC, PTEN | Gene carrying the variant | noise |
| 11 | Variant_Type | Genomic | categorical | Missense, Nonsense, Frameshift, Splice_site, Synonymous | Predicted molecular consequence | strong |
| 12 | Exon_Number | Genomic | numeric | 1–27 | Exon position | noise |
| 13 | In_Functional_Domain | Genomic | categorical | Yes, No | Variant falls in a known protein domain | strong |
| 14 | CADD_Phred | Genomic | numeric | 0–50 | CADD deleteriousness (≥ 20 = top 1%) | strong |
| 15 | REVEL_Score | Genomic | numeric | 0–1 | REVEL missense pathogenicity (≥ 0.5 suggestive) | strong |
| 16 | SIFT_Score | Genomic | numeric | 0–1 | SIFT (< 0.05 = damaging; **lower is worse**) | strong |
| 17 | PolyPhen2_Score | Genomic | numeric | 0–1 | PolyPhen-2 (≥ 0.85 probably damaging) | strong |
| 18 | SpliceAI_Score | Genomic | numeric | 0–1 | SpliceAI delta score (≥ 0.2 splice-altering) | strong |
| 19 | GERP_RS | Genomic | numeric | −12 to 6.2 | GERP++ conservation (> 2 conserved) | strong |
| 20 | PhyloP_100way | Genomic | numeric | −20 to 10 | PhyloP conservation, 100 vertebrates | strong |
| 21 | gnomAD_AF | Genomic | numeric | 1e-7 to 0.5 | Population allele frequency (ACMG BA1 > 5%, BS1 > 1%, PM2 rare) | strong (pathogenic = rarer) |
| 22 | Variant_Allele_Freq | Biomarker | numeric | 0.02–1 | Fraction of reads carrying the variant | moderate |
| 23 | Read_Depth | Biomarker | numeric | 20–1000 | Sequencing depth at the locus | noise |
| 24 | Tumor_Mutational_Burden | Biomarker | numeric | 0–60 mut/Mb | Tumour mutational burden | moderate |
| 25 | Ki67_Index | Biomarker | numeric | 0–100 % | Proliferation index | moderate |
| 26 | PD_L1_TPS | Biomarker | numeric | 0–100 % | PD-L1 tumour proportion score | noise |
| 27 | CEA_ng_mL | Biomarker | numeric | 0.1–200 ng/mL | Carcinoembryonic antigen (log-normal) | weak |
| 28 | CA125_U_mL | Biomarker | numeric | 1–2000 U/mL | Cancer antigen 125 (log-normal) | weak |
| 29 | HRD_Score | Biomarker | numeric | 0–100 | Homologous-recombination deficiency score | strong |
| 30 | Classification | Target | categorical | Benign 70%, Pathogenic 20%, VUS 10% | Clinical classification | target |

## How the synthetic signal was generated
* Each variant has a hidden *latent pathogenicity*: 1 for Pathogenic, 0 for Benign, and intermediate values for the VUS, about 35% of which are hidden-Pathogenic.
* Informative features shift their mean with the latent value. The noise features are independent of it.
* Feature noise is scaled 3.5×, and 6.5% of labelled rows carry the other class's biology (like historic misclassification). Together these keep a well-regularised model near 90% accuracy instead of about 100%.
* Missing cells are chosen uniformly at random (MCAR), 13% of all cells. The ID and target columns are always complete.
